title: RFID Smart Door MONSTER
tagline: Swipe your badge to enter! Read 13.56MHz crypto tags with SPI and unlock physical servo deadbolts.

phases.instructions: Collect the RC522 13.56MHz RFID Reader/Writer module, RFID white card, blue RFID keyfob, SG90 servo, and buzzer.
verificationCheckpoints: RC522 module with 8 header pins ready
RFID white card and blue keyfob ready

phases.instructions: CRITICAL: Connect RC522 VCC to 3.3V ONLY (NEVER 5V or you will fry the chip!). Connect SPI pins: MOSI to 11, MISO to 12, SCK to 13, SDA/SS to 10, RST to 9.
STOP AND DOUBLE CHECK: Verify with your eyes that the RC522 red wire goes into the Arduino '3.3V' socket, NOT '5V'.
verificationCheckpoints: No bridged solder connections on RC522 header

phases.instructions: Review how the MFRC522 library queries tag UIDs and checks against authorized master card credentials.
phases.codeExplanation:
- SPI.begin() initializes high-speed hardware SPI clock and data lines.
- mfrc522.PICC_ReadCardSerial() reads the 4-byte or 7-byte unique identifier (UID) from the tag.
- The loop compares the scanned UID byte-by-byte with masterUID.
- If matched, the deadbolt rotates 90 degrees for 3 seconds.
verificationCheckpoints: Understand how 13.56 MHz electromagnetic coupling powers passive tag chip

phases.instructions: Upload sketch and tap your card to serial monitor to view its unique UID. Update the masterUID array with your card's numbers and re-upload to unlock your door!
verificationCheckpoints: Serial monitor prints card UID hex values

phases.instructions: Access Granted! You built a commercial-grade contactless RFID security gate.
verificationCheckpoints: Ready to claim RFID Guardian badge

story: Build a high-security Contactless RFID monster lock! Read 13.56 MHz Mifare RFID cards and keyfobs over the SPI bus, authorize authorized serial badges, and actuate a micro-servo deadbolt.

troubleshooting.symptom: RFID reader does not detect cards at all
troubleshooting.cause: VCC wire plugged into 5V (which can damage chip) or poor SPI connection on Pin 13
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure VCC is plugged into 3.3V and check that SCK pin is securely connected to Pin 13.
diagnosticSteps: Check RC522 VCC wire: strictly 3.3V (5V will damage it).
Inspect SPI jumper connections: MOSI 11, MISO 12, SCK 13.
